clue.text: Liberal visiting plotters annoyed revolutionary Spanish gentlemen

indicators.note: visiting puts the Liberal in among the plotters, as a guest drops in

parts.note: a cabal is a secret group of plotters

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word for annoyed is read backwards

parts.note: annoyed means sore

explanation.surface: A political tale: a Liberal drops in on a group of conspirators who are furious with some Spanish rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like it describes the Spanish gentlemen, but it is the reversal signal; 'visiting' places the Liberal among the plotters.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is the Spanish word for a gentleman or horseman, used in English for a Spanish gent.

clue.text: Tapestry at first children weave

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word tapestry

parts.note: first letter of Tapestry
issue means offspring, children

explanation.surface: Instructions for a craft lesson: children start on a tapestry by weaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A tissue is a fine woven fabric, so the word can stand for a weave or web of threads.

clue.text: One doubting sign coat needs replacing

indicators.note: needs replacing says the letters of sign coat must be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure whether a sign coat, perhaps a painted board, must be redone.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic is a person who doubts or withholds belief about the existence of God.

clue.text: Monitor broadcast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to check or vet; also a display monitor
second meaning: to show on television

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that look like a TV-room pairing are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: One can screen people to vet them, and a channel screens a programme when it airs it.

clue.text: Vehicle, silver, in the old city

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: in says the silver sits inside the word the

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A list of items, a vehicle and some silver, found in an ancient city by excavators.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the clue into a vehicle, then silver tucked into the word 'the', which the surface reads as a plain article.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was the ancient Phoenician city in North Africa destroyed by Rome.

clue.text: Push five to quit Oxford?

indicators.note: to quit says the five leaves the word for push

parts.note: to shove is to push
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about forcing five students out of Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is not the university here: an oxford is a laced shoe, so the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxford is a style of laced leather shoe, so it is one example of the answer.

clue.text: University bookworm's obsession?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the University of ..., in the English town of that name
second meaning: what a keen reader loves doing

explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a university town west of London; the second half plays on the everyday word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is a town with a university, and perusing books is what a bookworm cannot stop doing.

clue.text: Having acceptable opinions, like a Conservative?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: holding sound, sensible views
second meaning, taken literally: thinking from the political right

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading: a Conservative's thinking is of the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-thinking people hold views most would call proper, and a Tory literally thinks on the right wing.

clue.text: Long to board Greek island trains

indicators.note: to board means to get on, so the word for long goes inside the island's name

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A traveller is yearning to catch a ferry to a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' looks like rail transport but is the verb: a coach trains athletes.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to tutor or instruct, so a sports coach trains a team.

clue.text: Pete blunders, stupidly purchasing small undergarment

indicators.note: purchasing here means taking in, so the jumble holds the small letter
stupidly says the letters of Pete blunders are jumbled foolishly

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Pete makes a fool of himself buying a small item of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender belt is an item of women's lingerie worn round the waist to hold up stockings.

clue.text: PM, happy individual after socialist's left discontented

indicators.note: after places the individual behind the socialist's remaining letters

parts.note: glad means happy

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of contents, leaving only the outer letters of socialist

parts.note: outer letters of socialist
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister is pleased to see a single figure feel let down after a socialist has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' reads as unhappy but means emptied of its contents, leaving just the two outer letters of the socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was a Liberal British Prime Minister four times in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Heard videoconferencing platform in business is fruitful

indicators.note: Heard says the platform's name is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: Microsoft Teams is a videoconferencing platform widely used in business

explanation.surface: Someone praises their office video-call software as productive.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to abound or be prolific, so something that teems is richly productive.

clue.text: Switching from American to English, actress Swinton's accent?

indicators.note: Switching from says one letter of the name is changed for another
to names the replacement letter that comes in

parts.note: Tilda Swinton is a Scottish actress

explanation.surface: Wonders whether Tilda Swinton changes her accent from American to English in a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accent' suggests her speaking voice, but it is the written mark; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is a diacritic, the wavy mark over a letter such as the Spanish ñ, and diacritics are called accents.

clue.text: Adult held by criminal in latest torment

indicators.note: held by puts the adult inside the jumbled letters
criminal says the letters of in latest are crooked, set in a new order

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A news item: an adult is held hostage by a criminal in the latest ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to tease or torment with something desired but kept out of reach.

clue.text: Press meets new heavy metal band

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes
maiden means new or first, as in a maiden voyage

explanation.surface: A reporter from the press meets a newly formed heavy metal band.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron Maiden is a famous English heavy metal group formed in the 1970s.

clue.text: Present work reduced for dissident

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

indicators.note: reduced says the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to tick is to work or function, as in what makes someone tick

explanation.surface: A rebel is given a gift of cut-down work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but means in attendance; tick for work is as in a clock that ticks.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds views at odds with accepted doctrine, a dissenter from orthodoxy.

clue.text: Pulling barrow over river, discovered that saves time

indicators.note: saves means keeps or holds, so the other letters contain time
over in a down clue means turned upward, so the word for barrow is read backwards

parts.note: a barrow is a hand cart

indicators.note: discovered means with the cover stripped, so river loses its outer letters

parts.note: the inner letters of river

explanation.surface: Someone drags a barrow across a river, finding a shortcut to save time.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means upwards, so the barrow reads from bottom to top; 'discovered' means with its cover, the outer letters, removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractive describes traction, the force used in drawing or hauling something along.

clue.text: Drug wayward son tried out, any number taken

indicators.note: wayward means going astray, so son tried is rearranged
taken, with out, says a letter is taken out of the jumbled letters

parts.note: N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: A wayward son experiments with drugs, taking any number of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange SON TRIED and take out ('out ... taken') the N for any number.
explanation.definitionFit: A steroid is a compound used as medication, often misused by athletes to build muscle.

clue.text: Son darts around quietly delivering fliers

indicators.note: around says the son and darts surround the quiet letter

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
arrows is another word for darts, the pub game
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A boy throws darts while quietly handing out leaflets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fliers' looks like leaflets, but means birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparrows are small birds, and birds are creatures that fly.

clue.text: Lost again badly, it brings wistful feelings

definitions.note: the answer is a single noun for such feelings

indicators.note: badly says the letters of lost again are put into a poor new order

explanation.surface: A fan whose team has lost again yearns for better days.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for the past, a bittersweet wistfulness.

clue.text: Elite golf competitor

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an entry is a competitor entered in a contest

explanation.surface: Describes a top-class golfer in a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the upper class, the well-born people just below the nobility.

clue.text: Poet's key verse essentially

parts.note: Home is a key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence, the heart, so the central letter of verse is taken

parts.note: the middle letter of verse

explanation.surface: A poet's key verse, the one that matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like an adjective, but it is the keyboard's Home key.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer was the ancient Greek epic poet credited with the Iliad and the Odyssey.

clue.text: Football club tries to limit heading for teenagers

indicators.note: to limit means to hem in, so the word for tries surrounds the letter

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case

indicators.note: heading for gives just the initial letter of teenagers

parts.note: first letter of teenagers

explanation.surface: A football club attempts to cap the number of teenagers it signs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts (Heart of Midlothian) is a Scottish football club in Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is the usual name for Heart of Midlothian, an Edinburgh football club.

clue.text: Turning a little heat up, nicking computer data

indicators.note: Turning says the hidden letters are read backwards
a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone turns up the heating a little, pilfering some warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is information fed into a computer for processing.

clue.text: Compassion and godliness with no end of benevolence

indicators.note: with no says the letter is dropped from the word for godliness

parts.note: piety means godliness, devoutness

indicators.note: end of gives only the last letter of benevolence

parts.note: last letter of benevolence

explanation.surface: A sermon theme: compassion and godliness, though without true goodwill.
explanation.definitionFit: Pity is sorrow felt for another's suffering, a form of sympathy.

clue.text: Bishop, extremely aghast, interrupts innocent story

indicators.note: interrupts says these letters break into the word for innocent

parts.note: naive means innocent, unworldly
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the first and last letters of aghast

parts.note: outer letters of aghast

explanation.surface: A bishop, deeply shocked, cuts into an innocent person's account.
explanation.walkthrough: RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title; with AT from 'aghast' it goes into NAIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, which is a tale.

clue.text: Recover from cleric having religious books, say, in retirement

indicators.note: in retirement means drawing back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a cleric
OT is the Old Testament, a set of religious books
eg (for example) is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A priest recovers in retirement surrounded by holy books.
explanation.definitionFit: To get over an illness or setback is to recover from it and move on.

clue.text: Most ineffectual method of proving mac's waterproof?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: most feeble or spineless, wet in the British sense
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Wet is British slang for feeble; a mac is a raincoat, and soaking one is a wet test.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet means weak and feeble in British slang, so the superlative describes the feeblest of all.
